answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each identity carries a visible history score; every action adds a pigment of proof that decays slowly if idle. New identities start near zero, so reaching the trust needed to transact requires real work over time — a cost of weeks, not tokens. An attacker spinning up thousands of identities pays that full latency per identity. A juniper-scented audit trail marks first actions, and a small ember of collateral is forfeited only on proven abuse.
